Graduate degree in public health, business administration, or related field.

Experience working on policy and legislative efforts and related projects.

Experience in team building, mentoring, and conflict resolution.
Experience in financial reporting in an academic environment for contracts and grants, private sponsors, and endowment funding.
Excellent critical thinking skills and strategic planning skills and experience.
Experience preparing, managing, and analyzing complex operational budgets with multiple funding streams and varying project periods.
Experience preparing, submitting, and managing research grants from different funding sources.

This position oversees and coordinates visible, complex, research grant programs/ initiatives, professional and public education/outreach activities, and training opportunities for undergraduate and graduate students and staff through subordinate supervisors, faculty, and other staff. The research portfolio contains topics related to firearm violence, social determinants of health, and the risk of firearm-related harm, political violence, and similar domains. It is responsible for the accountability and stewardship of human, financial, and physical resources in compliance with sponsor, departmental, and organizational goals and objectives. It is also responsible for supporting Centers-wide strategic planning and leading the implementation of projects that are critical to the mission of the Centers for Violence Prevention.
30% - Organizational Development
25% - Organizational Operations and Compliance
25% - Research Administration Support
20% - Strategic Project Implementation
High level of attention to detail and accuracy.
Demonstrated ability to build and support appropriate organizational structures, manage multiple concurrent responsibilities, and meet deadlines.

Working knowledge of policies, procedures, and regulations regarding cost accounting, supply chain, travel, intellectual property, conflict of interest requirements, publication rights, and/or protection of human subjects, preferably within the UCD or UCD Health context.
Excellent leadership skills and ability to build relationships and work collaboratively with a multi-disciplinary group of physicians, researchers, staff, and internal and external colleagues.
Working knowledge of various University of California systems including Aggie Enterprise, UC Path, Cayuse; and proposal submission portals for federal, state, and private sponsors.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to be convinced of opposing ideas by listening and processing alternative suggestions.
Ability to anticipate problems and challenges and proactively adapt.
Demonstrated ability to resolve conflicts and manage sensitive situations with discretion.
